Through CARE, comprehensive FGM and CM awareness programs reached 7,486 women and 5,598 men. Family days brought all family members together in safe, interactive spaces to discuss FGM and CM awareness, as well as positive parenting and gender roles program, which reached 501 community members. Men and boys were further engaged through sports and awareness events, reaching 5,143 participants. projects.description:
Recognizing the influence of religious discourse on social norms, targeted interventions sought to separate FGM from religious practices. BLESS and Al-Azhar capacitated 1516 religious leaders, including male priests and azhari school teachers on GBV, RH and FGM topics, the estimated number of the indirect beneficiaries is 45000 community members. 

CARE trained 403 religious leaders in cooperation with the Ministry of Endowments, 20 male community leaders to establish their networks, and 50 community volunteers and influencers. All were engaged as FGM advocates, working as agents of change and community leaders within their communities. In addition, 13 men’s networks were established, reaching 1,659 community members with comprehensive awareness activities.
The FGM–Humanitarian Initiative engaged 100 Sudanese community leaders to cascade knowledge and raise awareness within their communities, reaching a total of 3,800 community members. Adding to this, 2967 community members were reached through online post about the initiative.

projects.name: The provision of specialized health-care and psychological support response services is improved and expanded through the specialized Medical Response Clinics (Safe Women) addressing gender-based violence against women and girls and harmful practices with focus on FGM , provision of Post-Rape Kits and follow-up care
projects.description:
A total of 23 Safe Women Clinics are operational within university hospitals, providing integrated survivor-centered medical and psychosocial services. Across the reporting period, the university-based SWCs received a combined total of 1,611 cases of violence against women and girls across 16 governorates, reflecting sustained demand and utilization of specialized services. In parallel, Safe Women Clinics continued to play a critical role in prevention and community outreach. During the same period, a total of 347 health education sessions were delivered, reaching 9,680 women, and addressing GBV prevention, harmful practices, early identification of violence, and available referral and response services.
In addition to university hospitals, the SWC model has been significantly scaled through partnership with the Ministry of Health and Population (MOHP). A total of 65 Safe Women Clinics are now operational nationwide under MOHP, including 37 clinics established during the year, substantially expanding access to specialized GBV medical response services within public health facilities.

projects.name: Skills, knowledge, capacities and capabilities of government entities, youth-led organizations and networks, and local civil society organizations (CSOs) is enhanced to address negative social norms and promote women's empowerment
projects.description:
UNFPA-supported interventions strengthened the skills, knowledge, and institutional capacities of youth-led organizations and civil society partners to address negative social norms through structured, mandate-aligned capacity development and supported platforms for youth-led action. A total of 651 youth and young people were capacitated through partner-led mechanisms (472 through Etijah and 179 through Misr Foundation), with deliberate inclusion of 40 persons with disabilities, enhancing the readiness of youth cadres to act as facilitators, advocates, and community mobilizers.

Through Etijah, UNFPA strengthened the Population Awareness Clubs (PACs) delivery system by building the facilitation, leadership, and community engagement capacities of trained youth facilitators across governorates. Capacitated youth demonstrated improved competencies in participatory facilitation, edutainment-based engagement, and values-based dialogue on gender equality, reproductive health, family planning, the prevention of harmful practices, and violence against women and girls, supported by SOP-oriented trainings and refresher mechanisms to ensure quality and sustainability.

In parallel, implementation with Misr Foundation strategically strengthened youth capacities to address FGM medicalization by equipping youth—particularly within medical and advocacy cohorts—with evidence-based knowledge, ethical frameworks, and advocacy and communication skills to challenge harmful norms. Cinema- and arts-based methodologies were leveraged to support rights-based dialogue and youth-led norm change, including among youth with disabilities.

Complementing community-based capacity development, UNFPA strengthened youth psychosocial awareness and resilience as an enabling factor for sustained engagement on GBV prevention and social norm change. This included support to El-Nafsyea Podcast, which reached over 4 million people, and a structured digital mental health course targeting adolescents and youth, reinforcing stigma reduction, help-seeking behaviors, and informed participation in community dialogue.

Building on strengthened capacities, trained youth independently led large-scale outreach reaching over 720,000 community members and youth through integrated on-ground and digital engagement on GBVAWG, harmful practices (including FGM), reproductive health, and family planning. The scale and quality of youth-led dissemination demonstrate a clear transition from capacity development to functional youth leadership, contributing to sustained community-level engagement, increased dialogue on harmful norms, and strengthened local capacities to promote women’s empowerment and rights-based behaviors.

projects.description:
In Kafr El Sheikh Governorate, Decree No. 25683 was issued on 30 December 2025, formally establishing the Local Coordination Committee to Combat VAWG. Similarly, Menoufia Governorate issued Decree No. 1930 of 2025 on 30 December 2025, institutionalizing the Local Coordination Committee to Combat VAW. These decrees strengthen governance, clarify roles and responsibilities among stakeholders, and formalize referral pathways across health, protection, justice, and social service actors.

In parallel, six new governorates were selected for partnership to establish additional Local Coordination Committees—Beheira, Alexandria, South Sinai, Qalyubia, Menoufia, and Kafr El Sheikh—signaling continued geographic scale-up and national commitment to coordinated, localized responses. Collectively, these actions enhance the availability, accessibility, and quality of coordinated prevention and response services, particularly for girls and women at risk of FGM and child marriage.

projects.name: Livelihood and income generating programs are expanded for underpriviledged Egyptian and refugee women at risk of GBV against women and girls
projects.description:
In partnership with NCW, 1768 women were trained through GBV vocational and skills building initative. Female beneficiaries completed vocational program inclusive of awareness sessions on forms of GBV and were economically and psychologically empowered through sustaining provision of vocational skills’ training and psychological support sessions.

In partnership with Ministry of Youth and Sports and Etijah (national NGO), UNFPA supported 2,749 women and girls from refugee and host communities with livelihoods and vocational training. These sessions were delivered at 13 Women and Girls Safe Spaces across seven governorates in Egypt. It aimed to foster resilience by enhancing access to income generating opportunities. The sessions included various handicraft workshops such as sewing, hairdressing, and macrame and perfume-making. 

Lack of access to economic and livelihoods opportunities for refugee communities remained as the gap. These gaps are exacerbated by deep-seated trauma and systemic barriers for many refugee women. Without gender-responsive programming, livelihoods interventions can inadvertently heighten the risk of abuse. It is essential to integrate gender analysis into all economic empowerement and livelihoods initiatives to safeguard women at risk can safely access those opportunities.

projects.name: Support to national efforts to strengthen efficency of multi-sectoral coordination and GBV response through One Stop Shop Management Center(s) for women and girls exposed to violence
projects.description:
UNFPA continued to lead the UN collective technical assistance to the Government of Egypt in support of the implementation of the first One Stop Shop in Egypt, with a strong focus on strengthening multi-sectoral engagement under the leadership of the National Council for Women (NCW). Technical support prioritized coordination across relevant sectors and institutions, as well as the review and support to the endorsement of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) governing internal case intake and referral services within Cairo.

UNFPA also spearheaded a senior-level coordination meeting with NCW, resulting in a shared understanding and agreement on the OSC’s structure, floor layout, and service delivery model. A key contribution was ensuring that a survivor-centered approach is fully mainstreamed, positioning the Center as an emergency response entry point that facilitates timely and safe access to external social, legal, and medical services for GBV survivors. In parallel, UNFPA continued to advocate with national partners for the inclusion of refugee and migrant survivors, recognizing the need for context-sensitive approaches that mitigate potential protection risks, particularly for undocumented individuals.

projects.name: Anti violence against Women University Units are strengthend and expanded to offer prevention, response, referral and on-campus sensitization against gender-based violence including harmful practices and other prevelent forms of violence
projects.description:
A total of 486 members of Anti-Violence against Women (Anti-VAW) University Units were reached through capacity-building and coordination activities, strengthening university-based prevention, response, referral, and on-campus sensitization mechanisms to address gender-based violence, including harmful practices and technology-facilitated forms of violence.

A key milestone was the Eighth Annual Coordination Meeting for Anti-VAW University Units, held on 9 December in Cairo, which convened 115 participants (23 males and 92 females) from 16 governorates, with the support of the European Union and the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation. The meeting brought together university presidents and vice presidents, Anti-VAW Unit heads, students, and partners from the national referral pathway, reinforcing high-level commitment and cross-sectoral coordination. During the meeting, it was announced that the number of Anti-VAW University Units had expanded to 50 units nationwide, reflecting sustained scale-up and institutionalization within higher education institutions.

In parallel, 12 Anti-VAW University Units were provided with office equipment and furnishing, enhancing their operational readiness and visibility on campus. Collectively, these interventions strengthened universities as key entry points for survivor-centered response, referral to national services, and sustained awareness-raising, reinforcing a zero-tolerance approach to violence against women and girls within higher education institutions.
